narrative: Material PL1__M94BDDB7 exhibits erratic demand (CV 51.3%) with a mean of 4,643 units/day over 221 working days; combined with moderate lead time variability (CV 52.6%, mean 2.41 days), the sigma-LTD of 6,962 units demands a safety stock of 11,452 units to sustain a 95% service level — 255% above the current SAP setting of 3,222. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with EOQ order quantity of 27,316 units and reorder point of 22,663 units is recommended; peak inventory of 38,768 units remains within the 44,986-unit storage capacity. The additional annual holding cost of ~$2,005 is the economically necessary cost of service-level compliance.
warnings: Current SAP safety stock (3,222) covers only 0.46 sigma_LTD — significantly below the 1.645 sigma required for 95% service level.
Lead time CV of 52.6% classified as moderate instability — transport and supplier reliability improvements recommended.
1 demand outlier detected (0.5% of observations) — root cause investigation advised.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The material has non-zero daily demand (100% active days), high volume (~4,643 units/day), and erratic variability. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy is optimal as it triggers replenishment precisely when inventory position hits the reorder point, avoiding the excess holding cost of periodic-review systems while providing a fixed, EOQ-optimised order quantity that minimises total inventory costs.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Peak inventory at replenishment is 38,768 units against a 44,986-unit storage limit — 86.2% utilisation. No capacity cap binds under the recommended policy. However, any upward demand spike coinciding with a delayed replenishment could stress available space; a 10% demand surge would push peak inventory to ~41,500 units, still within capacity.
